case_title: Maloth Somaraju v. State of A.P.
high_court_outcome: Convicted of the offence u/s. 302 IPC and awarded sentence of life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the brother of the deceased, was alleged to have committed murder by inflicting fatal injuries with an axe on his elder brother during the night. The deceased was sleeping on a cot along with his son and wife. The wife, who was a close relative of the accused, witnessed the incident and reported it to the police. She provided detailed information in the FIR, which was filed shortly after the incident. The prosecution argued that the accused had a grudge against the deceased and that the wife's testimony was credible. The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court convicted him of murder under Section 302 of the IPC and sentenced him to life imprisonment. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's decision, finding that the wife's testimony was reliable and that the trial court had been influenced by irrelevant suspicious circumstances.
